LESSON: WRITING 1.3.1 HANDWRITING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why should we write neatly and legibly?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. outline characteristics of good handwriting for information
2. rewrite a short essay neatly and legibly for effective communication
3. assess handwritten texts for correct spelling and word spacing

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting makes your writing clear so others can read it easily.

• Look at the model your teacher shows. Notice shape, order, and spacing.

• Practise slowly first, then build neat speed.

• Check your work: Did you spell carefully? Did you use correct marks?

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Copy three model sentences neatly, leaving finger spaces between words.

Example 2: Spell five lesson words aloud, then write them without looking.

Example 3: Fix this sentence by adding capital letters and a full stop: “amina went to kisumu”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Write five neat sentences about your school using words from this topic.
2. Exchange books with a friend and check spelling or punctuation together.
3. Rewrite one messy sentence so it is clear and correct.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Complete a short guided paragraph in your exercise book.
2. List eight words from this topic and practise spelling them with a parent.
3. Write a short note to a friend using correct punctuation.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Discuss the characteristics of good handwriting,
2. Use the discussion findings to create a criteria or checklist for assessing good handwriting,
3. Rewrite a short essay on the theme using neat and legible handwriting and share with peers,
4. Assess each other’s work according to the criteria or checklist prepared for correct word spacing, neatness, and legibility,
5. Citizenship: This is promoted as the learner demonstrates tolerance when assessing other’s work according to the criteria or checklist prepared for correct word spacing, neatness and legibility.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we write neatly and legibly?
2. How can illegible handwriting result in miscommunication?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Neat writing helps the reader.
2. Check spelling and punctuation before you finish.
3. Practice a little every day.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
